definitions.gloss: main hall of a Shinto shrine
definitions.explanation: The innermost and most sacred building of a Shinto shrine, which houses the enshrined deity (御神体). Visitors typically worship at the worship hall (拝殿) in front, as the main hall is usually not open to the public.

examples.japanese: {本殿|ほんでん}は{国宝|こくほう}に{指定|してい}されている。
examples.english: The main hall is designated as a national treasure.

examples.japanese: {本殿|ほんでん}の{裏|うら}には{古|ふる}い{杉|すぎ}の{木|き}がある。
examples.english: Behind the main hall stands an old cedar tree.

examples.japanese: この{神社|じんじゃ}の{本殿|ほんでん}は{室町時代|むろまちじだい}に{建|た}てられたもので、{歴史的|れきしてき}{価値|かち}が{非常|ひじょう}に{高|たか}い。
examples.english: The main hall of this shrine was built during the Muromachi period and has extremely high historical value.

notes:
USAGE:
{本殿|ほんでん} refers specifically to the main building of a Shinto shrine ({神社|じんじゃ}), where the {御神体|ごしんたい} (sacred object representing the deity) is housed. It is distinct from the {拝殿|はいでん} (worship hall), where visitors pray.

The {本殿|ほんでん} is typically located behind the {拝殿|はいでん} and is often not accessible to the general public.

For Buddhist temples, the equivalent term is {本堂|ほんどう} (main hall).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本殿|ほんでん}を{参拝|さんぱい}する: to worship at the main hall
- {本殿|ほんでん}の{建築|けんちく}{様式|ようしき}: architectural style of the main hall
- {国宝|こくほう}の{本殿|ほんでん}: a main hall designated as a national treasure
